feedback.problem:
Determine the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].$

${a}_{32}^{′}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| & =2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|+(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(6-0)-0(-3-0)-1(1-0) \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{32}^{t}={c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2-0) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{32}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{1}{11}\cdot (-2) \\  & =-\frac{2}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$
